pr_title: fix(ivy): support SkipSelf when injecting ViewContainerRef, ElementRef and ChangeDetectorRef
pr_body:
Currently Ivy doesn't support adding `@SkipSelf` for some of the special DI tokens (e.g. `ViewContainerRef`, `ElementRef`, `ChangeDetectorRef`). These changes add support for it since it's something we support in ViewEngine.

Fixes #34066.
pr_comments: is this PR still relevant now that Andrew has #34839 in the merge queue?
I think so. #34839 handles `SkipSelf` only for the `Injector` token, whereas these changes do it for `ElementRef`, `ViewContainerRef` etc.
Rebased which removed the need to bump the size limit.

FYI, it turned out that adding support for `@Host` decorator required extracting common logic into separate functions. We discussed this with @crisbeto and agreed to cherry-pick the commit from this PR into #34839 and continue further review (and fixes if needed) as a part of #34839. Thank you.

issue_context.title: In Ivy, SkipSelf() is not accessing the parent's ViewContainerRef, ElementRef, etc
issue_context.body:
# 🐞 bug report ### Affected Package The issue is caused by Angular Ivy ### Description Before Ivy, I was able to access the `ViewContainerRef`, `ElementRef`, etc of the parent directive using the `@SkipSelf` decorator in the child directive. With Ivy integrated in my project, it's no longer skipping its own injections and accessing the ones in its parent. For example, I have the following code: In app.component.ts ```ts @Directive({ selector: '[parentDirective]' }) export class ParentDirective { constructor(private vc: ViewContainerRef){ console.log(vc.element); } } @Directive({ selector: '[childDirective]' }) export class ChildDirective { constructor(@SkipSelf() private vc: ViewContainerRef){ console.log(vc.element); } } ``` in app.component.html ```html
parent child
``` These two directive classes should log the same ViewContainerRef element. However, with Ivy, you can see that's no longer the case. Here is the [reproduction](https://ivy.ng-run.com/edit/xMfu7xoF1t4b8hFvoU9N?open=app%2Fapp.component.html). This reproduction is made in Angular Ivy 8.1.0-next.3. But I also see this behavior in my project that's on "@angular/core": "9.0.0-rc.3", ## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction [Minimal Reproduction](https://ivy.ng-run.com/edit/xMfu7xoF1t4b8hFvoU9N?open=app%2Fapp.component.html) ## 🌍 Your Environment **Angular Version:** 


"@angular/core": "9.0.0-rc.3",
comments: Note: When trying to fix this, we realized that it's non-trivial because of the way Ivy is architected. We should consider whether this is actually a feature we want long-term due to the design / performance cost.

@kara - RE "whether this is actually a feature we want long-term due to the design / performance cost" - Please see my comments on #39475

In short, [HostBindings not updated by detectChanges() in OnPush component](22560) (or detached components) is a real problem, and the workaround for that requires accessing the parent view's ChangeDetector. 

Personally I think the HostBindings update design is a root problem (it should be possible to update classes tied to property values without jumping through hoops or understanding things like "hostbindings aren't updated by a view's detectChanges()") - I don't know how many other common use-cases there are requiring core parameter types from the node's parent, but my guess is that if that design were fixed, the need for this would be dramatically reduced.

Also, if injectflags are not supported, there should be a compiler or runtime error.
FYI, this issue is resolved by #39464 and the fix will be available in v11.0.0. Thank you.

review_comments: One more thing to consider: when crossing component boundaries, we have to respect `@Host` config flags as well. In other words, if there are `@SkipSelf` and `@Host` flags used together, the `ViewContainerRef` should not be found if it would cross a component boundary.

@crisbeto I worked on a fix to support @SkipSelf for Injectors and noticed that `tNode.parent` may not be available when we cross component boundary, [see a test here](https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/34839/files#diff-881d964a81b3db8c8cb5311b8e3546ecR644). It looks like this code should be updated to handle this case as well ([similar to this line](https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/34839/files#diff-a29d4642602b40bdabe81990eed99e50R353)).

Hmm, would that be a problem for `ViewContainerRef`, `ChangeDetectorRef` and `ElementRef` though (crossing component boundaries)? A node should always be inside another element or a view container so we'd always resolve the value before we have to cross a component boundary. That being said, I might be missing some context here.

I believe @AndrewKushnir is talking about the case where the `child` element requesting `SkipSelf` is a `ViewChild` of `parent` instead of a `ContentChild`. 

```ts
@Component({selector: 'parent', template: '<child></child>' }) 
export class Parent {...}
```

If `child` is a root node of the `parent` template, `tNode.parent` would be null because the `parent` element is in a different view and we can't cross component boundaries with the `tNode` tree (because `tNode.parent` would change with each usage of the component).  So `ViewContainerRef` would not be found.

In this case, we should be falling back to the `T_HOST` saved in the `LView`:

```suggestion
            tNode.parent || lView[T_HOST}, getParentInjectorView(getParentInjectorLocation(tNode, lView), lView),
```
Can we add a test where the child element requesting `ViewContainerRef` is a ViewChild of the parent element?
